claims.text: Official uv docs define lock freshness as the lockfile matching project metadata (pyproject.toml). Adding a dependency, or changing a constraint so the locked version is excluded, makes it outdated; a constraint that still includes the locked version does not. New upstream releases do NOT make a lockfile outdated. `uv lock --check` tests freshness and is documented as equivalent to --locked for other commands.

evidence.locator: 'Checking the lockfile' and 'Automatic lock and sync (--locked, --frozen)' sections (fetched via WebFetch summary, not verbatim page text)

claims.text: --locked: if the lockfile is missing or out of date, uv exits with an error instead of updating it (it checks freshness, never rewrites the lock).

--frozen: uses the lockfile as the source of truth without checking whether it is up to date against pyproject.toml; no re-lock. If pyproject.toml and uv.lock disagree, uv will install what the lock says without error. (Missing lockfile presumably errors; not verified in the fetched text.)

No, not per the retrieved docs. The sync concept page says nothing about network behavior for either flag. --locked still needs to resolve nothing but installation still fetches packages not in the cache; --frozen skips lock check/update but still downloads wheels/sdists if not cached. Network restriction is a separate control: --offline ('only use locally cached data and locally available files'). Inference: guaranteeing no network requires --offline plus a populated cache or local index; I did not test this.

`uv sync` is exact by default: it removes packages in the environment that are not in the lockfile. Use `uv sync --inexact` to keep extraneous packages. `uv run` defaults the opposite (inexact); `uv run --exact` makes it exact.

Recommendation (policy, not sourced fact): In CI, gate with `uv lock --check` or `uv sync --locked`, so a stale lock fails the build. In production deploy/image builds, run `uv sync --locked` (add `--no-dev` and other group flags as appropriate), keeping the default exact sync so the environment matches the lock. Use --frozen only where the lock was already validated in CI and the build context lacks metadata/needs speed (e.g. layered Docker builds), accepting that drift goes undetected. Add --offline with a pre-populated cache/internal index only if network isolation is required. Avoid --inexact in production unless extras are intentionally managed.
